description: The perfect sugar cookies recipe that won't spread!!!! This will make about 12 cookies depending on size!  #nospreadcookies #nospreadsugarcookies #sugarcookierecipe #sugarcookiesoftiktok #decoratedsugarcookies   No spread sugar cookies recipe, Christmas sugar cookies, decorate Christmas sugar cookies, Christmas sugar cookie recipe
transcript: One of the biggest traditions around Christmas is baking and decorating your own sugar cookies so I'm here to give you the best sugar cookie recipe that will not spread for you this holiday season. We're starting off with unsalted butter that is at room temperature. This is what it should look like. It shouldn't be melting but you should be able to squeeze it and it holds its shape and we're adding one cup into our mixer and we're gonna cream that. Once that creams for just a few seconds maybe even a minute at max we're gonna scrape down that bowl and then we're gonna add in one cup of granulated white sugar. We're gonna cream that together for about two to three minutes until you have a nice light and fluffy consistency. Scraping the bowl again and then we're gonna add in one cold egg straight from the refrigerator, one teaspoon of salt, and one tablespoon of butter vanilla. You can use any extract you want, almond, vanilla, anything you want. We're just mixing that until combined and then scraping the bowl again when we're gonna add in three cups of flour and I like to add it in increments so about two cups at once. Mix it and then add the additional cup after that. If you live in a high humidity area like I do you may need more flour. You want the dough to be pulling from the sides of the bowl like so so keep adding just a little bit of flour until you achieve that. Then we're gonna dump out the dough onto a piece of parchment paper. We're putting another piece of parchment paper over it and rolling it out to 10 millimeters. If you don't have a measuring rolling pin like I do just roll it out to the best of your ability evenly. We're then gonna put it in the fridge for about 30 to 45 minutes covered and then we're ready to cut out our shapes. I'm just doing a bow because I actually have an order to do so we're doing this bow and it's gonna come out super easily. I prefer to use a perforated cookie sheet but you can also use parchment paper if that's all you have. It will work just as good. The back just won't be as fancy and delicate looking. Then we're gonna poke a few holes in it with a scribe or toothpick. The toothpick will work just fine. I bake these at 335 for seven minutes and then I turn the tray around and I bake for another seven eight minutes. The baking time and the baking temperature may vary based on the type of oven you have and the way your oven is working. This is also dependent on how you want your cookie baked if you want a soft cookie or if you want more of a well done cookie that's a little bit crunchy. I like the bottoms of mine to be barely brown or a little bit of brown and this is how I check. I usually take a spatula that has holes in it and I'll look at the bottom. I'll flip it over make sure it's done to how I want it to be done and then I flatten it with a fondant tool but you can use a bottom of a cup or anything you wish. Once they're cooled off you're ready to decorate so enjoy this recipe and have a very merry Christmas.
